purpose: Translate conformance command JSON into the public Rust Command API.
behavior: Requires a nonempty string argv array and maps nullable env entries to removals, alongside cwd, inheritance, timeout, grace, text, merge, verbatim, input, output cap, stdin and PTY options.

Duration conversion uses Duration::from_millis when as_u64 succeeds; otherwise only finite, nonnegative as_f64 values proceed to Duration::from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0), without an upper representable-range guard. PTY objects default to 80 by 24 and require dimensions representable as u16.
Accepts text or whitespace-stripped hex input; rejects unknown command options as harness errors.
contracts: The scenario vocabulary is shared with TypeScript, but representability failures require language-restricted scenarios.
dependencies: api/command.rs supplies the builder setters; runner/schema.rs must validate syntactic shapes before translation.
failures_or_limits: This adapter does not expose maxRssBytes or pipe backpressure at this source revision. hex_bytes consumes pairs and accepts a final single hex digit; schema.rs reuses the same parser rather than requiring even length.

A sufficiently large finite nonnegative value on the floating-point duration branch can exceed Duration's representable range and reach the panicking Duration::from_secs_f64 conversion instead of returning this adapter's Err. schema.rs accepts numeric timeoutMs/graceMs options without that upper bound; this is a source/API boundary, not an observed panic.

purpose: Compare conformance outcomes while separating product mismatches from invalid harness expectations.
behavior: Models exit/run fields, output data, pieces and process entries with typed values; errors can be checked by code, message fragments and partial result.

Only Fail::Product is eligible for pending under the suite's other conditions. An absent ordinary field in the returned field map becomes Fail::Harness through string conversion, whereas an expected partial result absent from Error::result() explicitly yields Fail::Product. Malformed expectation shapes are checked during Scenario::load through Names::step and schema::step/schema::expect (including pieces/entries validation), with load errors classified as Harness; the comparator alone is not the complete shape validator.

Numeric matchers support bounds and null, text matchers support literals, containment, regex, length and hex; process inventories require an unordered one-to-one assignment rather than a greedy match.
contracts: Text length counts characters while binary output length counts bytes; listed expectation fields are mandatory observations.
dependencies: types.rs and Error supply outcomes; runner/pattern.rs defines the regex subset.
failures_or_limits: Recursive inventory matching may explore multiple assignments for overlapping predicates; this is test-source logic, not evidence of executed conformance.

purpose: Parse the pending conformance ledger and reject unknown or stale waivers.
behavior: Trims lines, ignores blank and full-line comments, and requires exactly an item identifier and a work-package token.
Rejects duplicate entries and malformed identifier/work-package syntax.
Checks pending identifiers against known contract items and flags a waiver as stale once all applicable scenarios for that item passed.
contracts: Pending is item-level: the item identifier precedes the first dot in a scenario ID.
dependencies: runner/suite.rs provides known items and aggregated applicable scenario results.
failures_or_limits: Although the introductory syntax description mentions comments, the parser only ignores lines beginning with #; inline trailing comment tokens fail. A pending record is not a runtime guarantee.

purpose: Execute the conformance scenario DSL with named children, runs, readers and captures.
behavior: Creates fresh scenario variables and temporary files, runs actions sequentially, then cancels the shared token, aborts run tasks, drops children and attempts directory removal.
Applies a default ten-second per-step deadline; OS-oracle timeouts are harness failures while other action timeouts are product failures.
Supports synchronous or named asynchronous run, pipe/PTY spawn, write/read/wait/stop/resize/process inventory, shared abort, and independently observed OS liveness.
Variable substitution returns an array for an exact multivalue reference and uses the first value when embedded in text.
contracts: Named asynchronous runs use spawn_local; PTY stdin cannot be closed through the pipe write action.
dependencies: runner/command.rs builds public Commands; read.rs retains readers; os.rs checks PIDs independently; expect.rs compares outcomes.
failures_or_limits: Fixture paths are joined to the scenario temporary directory; this is a trusted test DSL rather than a path containment boundary. Cleanup aborts tasks without claiming an observed tree-gone result.

purpose: Preflight scenario names, variable references and handle-kind constraints before execution.
behavior: Seeds FIXTURE, TMP and EXE, validates file contents and every action schema, and requires references to existing child or run names.
Requires as for await:false runs, validates PTY resize dimensions, forbids terminal stdin close, and checks OS PID references.
Validates non-expectation variable uses before defining new captures; the current step expectation can refer to captures introduced by that step.
contracts: Spawn handle kind is inferred from options.pty and recorded with a derived name.pid variable.
dependencies: runner/schema.rs checks field values; runner/scenario.rs invokes preflight while loading.
failures_or_limits: Reusing a name overwrites its table entry rather than being rejected. Static declaration of a child does not establish that the runtime spawn succeeded.

purpose: Provide independent operating-system PID liveness observations for contract scenarios.
behavior: Classifies Linux proc states and macOS ps output, treating zombies as dead; on Windows it checks tasklist CSV and its no-task informational response.
Uses three outcomes, Alive, Dead and Unknown; an unreadable or ambiguous observation is a harness failure, never evidence of death.
Polls spawn_blocking observations every twenty milliseconds until the requested state or deadline, then distinguishes product mismatch from oracle failure.
contracts: The oracle must be independent of Omni process inventory.
dependencies: Platform /proc, ps and tasklist boundaries; runner/mod.rs resolves PID inputs and consumes the result.
failures_or_limits: Observations identify PID numbers without a captured creation identity, so PID reuse can appear as a still-live process. The source also creates canonical per-scenario temp directories but does not itself run scenarios.

purpose: Restrict and normalize conformance regexes to the intended JavaScript-u/Rust common subset.
behavior: Rewrites digit and word shorthands to ASCII classes and dot to exclude LF, CR, U+2028 and U+2029.

Supports selected escapes, groups, alternatives and quantifiers, while rejecting lookaround, inline flags, backreferences, Unicode property/space escapes, surrogate escapes and ambiguous class constructs.
Tracks whether quantifiers have an atom, permits a single lazy modifier, and finishes with Rust Regex parsing.
contracts: Cross-language equivalence is claimed only for patterns accepted by this restricted grammar.
dependencies: regex crate compiles the normalized expression; conformance/regex-table.json supplies shared differential fixtures.
failures_or_limits: The implementation is a validator and rewriter, not support for general JavaScript regular expressions. No differential fixtures were executed in this analysis.

purpose: Read conformance child output across steps while preserving line fragments, capture state and loss metrics.
behavior: Keeps a stream reader plus pending stdout/stderr/PTY fragments; chunk mode splits complete lines for captures and line mode reassembles continued pieces.
Captures the first regex group or whole match and can stop after a required number of matching complete lines; it consumes the entire current item even after reaching that count.
Flushes partial text at gaps and EOF, fails an unsatisfied match count, returns per-step output and pieces plus dropped-byte observations, and optionally detaches the reader.
contracts: A reused reader keeps its mode; switching modes attempts a fresh public stream claim, subject to single-consumer rules.
dependencies: io stream APIs provide chunks/lines and loss counters; runner/pattern.rs compiles captures; runner/mod.rs stores variables.
failures_or_limits: Capture totals and pending fragments persist across steps whereas returned output is per-read. Explicit detach drops the source, so the product consumer cannot later be reclaimed.

purpose: Load scenario files with strict identifiers, action keys and platform/language filters.
behavior: Requires a filename-matching C-category-number.suffix ID, rejects unknown top-level fields, and validates optional nonempty OS/language lists against allowed names.
Requires a nonempty steps array and preflights all variable/handle names before applicability selection.
Recognizes exactly ten action names and their permitted additional fields, with timeoutMs available to every action.
contracts: Exactly one action must appear per step; absent platform or language filters apply universally.
dependencies: runner/names.rs validates references and shapes; suite.rs selects current-platform Rust scenarios after loading.
failures_or_limits: Platform filtering does not bypass structural validation during load. This file declares selection rules but provides no execution result.
